dataset_name: Delhi Hourly Electricity Demand and Weather Series (2-Year Synthetic)

spec_compliance.data_mode_requirement: Strictly flagged as DEMONSTRATION / SYNTHETIC. Must never be passed silently as real.

summer_daily_peaks.peak_1_afternoon: 15:00 - 15:30 (Commercial HVAC, office demand, peak ambient heatwave)
summer_daily_peaks.peak_2_night: 23:00 - 00:00 (Residential bedroom AC cooling during hot nights)

winter_daily_profile.shape: Flatter curve with evening heating peak and no afternoon cooling spike

seasonal_progression.pre_monsoon_ramp_up: March to June: soaring temperatures induce intense AC cooling demand
seasonal_progression.monsoon_dip: July to September: rain cooling and persistent cloud cover reduce daytime AC demand
seasonal_progression.autumn_brief_rise: October: clear post-monsoon warmth and pre-festive commercial activities
seasonal_progression.winter_low: December to February: lowest baseload and moderate evening heating

weekday_vs_weekend.rationale: Commercial institutions, schools, and offices observe reduced weekend operations

noise_model.noise_type: Autocorrelated Gaussian noise with 3-hour moving average

disclaimer: CRITICAL: This dataset contains SYNTHETIC simulation data designed for offline demonstration, machine learning testing, and system verification. Per system architectural guidelines, synthetic data must never be presented or published as official Delhi SLDC electricity telemetry.
